title: Where does sunlight go when it reaches Earth?
group: HOWN — How and Why in Nature
examples: How much sunlight does Earth reflect?
Why does melting ice make Earth warmer?
Does the Sun heat the air directly?

explain.say: Out of every 100 units of sunlight reaching the top of the atmosphere, not all of it warms our planet. Let's follow where it goes.

draw.text: Where does sunlight go when it reaches Earth?

explain.say: About 23 units bounce straight back to space off clouds, dust and the air itself. Bright white clouds are especially good mirrors.
About 23 units are absorbed in the atmosphere, by water vapour, dust and ozone, and warm the air.

The biggest share, about 47 units, is soaked up by land and oceans, which warm up and then heat the air from below. Another 7 bounce off bright surfaces like ice, snow and desert, so when ice melts, Earth absorbs more.

faq.q: How much sunlight does Earth reflect?
faq.a: About 30 percent of the sunlight reaching Earth is reflected straight back to space, mostly by clouds, and the rest by the air, ice, snow and other bright surfaces. Scientists call this Earth's albedo.

faq.q: Why do clouds reflect so much sunlight?
faq.a: Clouds are made of countless tiny droplets whose surfaces scatter light in all directions, so thick clouds bounce much of the sunlight back to space. That is one reason cloudy days are cooler.

faq.q: Why does melting ice warm the Earth more?
faq.a: Ice and snow reflect most sunlight, but dark ocean or land absorbs most of it. When ice melts, the darker surface underneath soaks up more heat, causing more melting.
asks: What is the ice albedo effect?

faq.q: Where does the heat go in the end?
faq.a: Earth sends the energy back out to space as invisible infrared heat. Greenhouse gases like carbon dioxide and water vapour hold some of it in, keeping Earth warm enough for life.
asks: Why doesn't Earth keep getting hotter?

faq.q: Does the Sun heat the air directly?
faq.a: Only partly. Air lets most sunlight pass through, so the Sun warms land and sea first, and they warm the air above them. That is why air is usually warmest near the ground.
asks: How does the Sun warm the air?

facts: Earth reflects about 30 percent of incoming sunlight back to space.
Fresh snow can reflect around 80 to 90 percent of sunlight, while open ocean reflects less than 10 percent.

quiz.say: What takes the largest share of the sunlight reaching Earth?
quiz.show: The biggest share of sunlight is…

options.show: Used by plants to make food
options.say: Used by plants to make food

quiz.why: About 47 percent of incoming sunlight is absorbed by the surface, more than any other share.

wrong.1: Air, clouds and dust reflect about 23 percent, a smaller share.
wrong.2: Plants use only a tiny fraction of sunlight for photosynthesis.
